notes.title: Captain Blood – Patch Update Now Live!
notes.notes:
Ahoy, Captains! 

First off, we want to send a massive thank you to our community. Your feedback, bugs reports, and support have been invaluable in helping us shape and improve [i]Captain Blood[/i]. We’ve read your comments, checked your reports, and truly appreciate your patience as we worked on this patch. Our goal was to tackle as many issues as possible in one solid update — and now, it's here!

Here’s what’s been improved in this update:

* Fixed voice-over  issues
* Corrected button glyphs 
* Main menu now plays the correct music
* Resolved crashes after visiting the shop in Episodes 9 & 36
* Fixed overflow in Control Settings - Quick Attack and Strong Attack 
* QTE interaction icons now properly aligned
* No more floating grass in Episode 17 QTE
* Fixed ship lighting in the prologue cutscene
* Tackled cannon control navigation issues
* Widescreen support is now fixed
* Resolved vibration issues
* UI now displays correctly for Deutsch and Magyar
* Eliminated 1px shift in controller image
* Fixed sea flickering and reflection in Episode 20
* Fixed issue with default gun firing during Execution 1
* Repaired hitting sound effect
* Checkpoints restart correctly after a missed QTE
* “Profile Saved” text no longer overflows
* Fixed double selection highlight in Character Controls settings
* Fixed crashes and freeze issues on boot-up 
* Improved FPS during Bombardier’s Execution
* Fixed missing resources in Episodes 7–9
* Fixed incorrect price label for the first item in the Shop
* Pistol upgrade now works as intended
* Corrected combo info in Shop
* Fixed hair physics collisions in the main menu
* Subtitle issues resolved
* Machine gun audio glitch squashed
* Fixed overall sound effects issue
* Motion blur ghosting fixed
* High-res texture issues resolved
* No more stretched logo
* Fixed non-random loading screen hints
* Fixed mouse sensitivity 
* Corrected wrong button prompts
* Fixed English-only display of "Alternative" and "Original" in Settings
* Monitor and display settings now function correctly
* Sail lighting fixed
* Resolved issues selecting disconnected displays
* Thai localization corrected
* Pause menu glitches fixed
* Sea battle progress bar now works (Ch. 6 & 18)
* Fixed missing QTE fail icon
* Upgrade descriptions in Shop menu no longer overlap
* Various shadow and miscellaneous image fixes
* Numerous small UI tweaks (menus, pause, Shop, etc.)
* Removed excess grass in Ch. 5 Ep. 17 finishing cutscene
* Updated and fixed credits video (no more crash!)
* Updated Shop videos
* Updated title screens
* Added support for multiple gamepad glyphs
* Additional vibration feedback added

Once again, thank you for sailing with us, sharing your experiences, and helping make [i]Captain Blood[/i] a better game.

notes.title: Demo patch #2
notes.notes:
[b]Ahoy everyone! [/b]

As we sail closer to the game’s release, we’ve updated the demo to better reflect its state and the new technologies in it: x64 architecture, modern rendering APIs (DirectX 12 by default, with Vulkan available via an .ini file), a physics engine adapted to the new systems, and a range of smaller quality-of-life improvements.

We’d love for you to give it a try and share your thoughts—it really helps us fine-tune the game for launch. And for those of you playing on a Steam Deck, this build is optimized for it, so we’re especially interested in hearing how it runs for you.

Thanks a ton for being part of this journey with us!

[i]Kindest regards,
SNEG Team[/i]

notes.title: Captain Blood, a hack-and-slash pirate game revealed in 2004, will finally release in 2024
notes.notes:
Way back in 2004, that terrible year when I swore off video games entirely to focus on my university studies, developers 1C SeaWolf announced Captain Blood, a piratical action game loosely based on Rafael Sabatini's adventure novels, in which a crew of 17th century freebooters set forth across the Spanish Main to rescue a magistrate's daughter from assorted bilge-drinking scallywags. Early footage painted the portrait of a spirited 3D hack-and-slasher featuring much buckling of swashes, heaving of hos and jollying of rogers.

Jim Rossignol (RPS in peace) was cautiously enthused when he played Captain Blood in 2008. "It was actually pretty fun - especially the arcade boat violence between speedy galleons - but I'm not exactly holding out for a masterpiece," he wrote. Alas, Captain Blood's ship struck a reef in the shape of unspecified publishing disputes, and sank beneath the waves after one last defiant preview showing in 2010. Now, the game has risen from the depths Flying Dutchman-style thanks to new developers Seawolf Studio and General Arcade and publisher SNEG Ltd. It'll finally launch on PC later this year.
